 In The Supreme Court Of India

RAKESH CHAND ALIAS RAKESH KUMAR App
VERSUS  STATE OF HIMACHAL PRADESH Res  O R D E R Leave granted.
This appeal challenges the judgment and order dated 28.11.2025 passed by the High Court of Himachal Pradesh at Shimla, in Cr.M.P.(M) No. 1505/2025.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant herein has been booked for the crime registered pursuant to FIR No. 03/2024 dated 08.03.2024 registered at Police Station Bagga, District Solan, Himachal Pradesh with respect to offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(f) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and Section 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act).

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: An application seeking regular bail having been rejected by the High Court vide impugned order dated 28.11.2025, the appellant has preferred the instant appeal.
This Court vide its order dated 09.01.2026 issued notice in the instant matter and also directed that no coercive steps be taken against the appellant till the next date of hearing.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant in support of the appeal and learned counsel for the State and perused the material on record.

Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that in Cr.M.P.(M) No. 1505/2025, out of which, this appeal arises, the appellant had the interim protection during the pendency of the said matter before the High Court.
However, the High Court dismissed the said case and directed the appellant herein to surrender failing which steps would be taken to secure his presence as per law.

Being aggrieved by the said order, the appellant has filed this appeal and this Court by interim order dated 09.01.2026 has granted interim protection to the appellant herein subject to certain terms and conditions; that the appellant has been cooperating in the trial and as many as nine out of seventeen witnesses have been examined.
The interim order has been in force since 09.01.2026.

sentences.text: He further submitted that the appellant is willing to abide by the terms and conditions that may be imposed while granting the relief of bail to him.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent-State with reference to the counter affidavit contended that the appellant is none other than the step-father of the victim girl; that the allegations against the appellant herein are not only under the provisions of the Indian Penal Code but also under Section 6 of the POCSO Act; that the trial is in progress and any relief being granted to the appellant herein would frustrate the trial inasmuch the appellant as well as the victim reside in the same house and therefore no relief may be granted to the appellant herein and the interim protection may also be vacated.

In response to this submission, appellants counsel submitted that the appellant would not reside in the same house in which the victim is residing and he would not make any attempt to approach the victim or her mother in any manner during the pendency of the trial and any other condition may be imposed on the appellant while granting him the relief.
We take note of the aforesaid submissions, we find that the appellant had interim protection during the pendency of the case before the High Court but subsequently, the bail was rejected.
Hence, we allow the appeal.
In the circumstances, we make the interim order dated 09.01.2026 absolute.

For ease of reference, the said interim order is extracted as under:
Issue notice to the respondent, returnable on 06.02.2026.
Learned counsel for the petitioner is also permitted to serve the standing counsel for the respondent/State.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that since, July, 2025, the petitioner has had the benefit of the interim order granted by the High Court.
However, in view of the impugned order, the interim order also stood vacated in November, 2025.
The petitioner has preferred this petition on 11.12.2025.
In the circumstances, interim protection may be extended to the petitioner herein.
Taking note of the aforesaid facts and submission, we direct that no coercive steps shall be taken against the petitioner herein, till the next date of hearing.

We, therefore, allow this appeal and direct as under:
The appellant shall be produced before the concerned Trial Court as early as possible and the Trial Court shall release him on bail, subject to such conditions as it may deem appropriate to impose to ensure his presence in the proceedings arising out of FIR No. 03/2024 mentioned above.
It is directed that the appellant shall extend complete cooperation in the trial of the instant case.
The appellant shall not misuse his liberty in any manner.
The appellant shall not make any attempt to approach the victim or her mother during the pendency of the trial.
